newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 9.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.

- European Commission sources and Irish government ministers say they do not expect the European Union to force Ireland to introduce charges for domestic water supply, despite claims to the contrary from opposition party, The Progressive Democrats.
- Ireland's three coalition leaders have decided to wait until the end of April before fixing a date for the general election.
- A burial ground dating from before 1800 has been uncovered at a building site in Rathfarnham in the south of Dublin city.

- Doubts over Germany's ability to enter European economic and monetary union (EMU) resurfaced on Tuesday as new unemployment data was seized on by speakers at a jobs "summit" to warn that Germany may yet miss the boat in 1999.
- Irish diplomats and EU officials on Tuesday denied claims by Progressive Democrat leader Mary Harney that metering of water would have to be introduced here.
- An Irish couple who claimed their lives became hell when rumours started circulating that they had won a 0.5 million Irish pounds jackpot were compensated by Ireland's National Lottery on Tuesday.
- The Irish pound slipped back further on currency markets on Tuesday as sterling established new levels above 2.78 German marks.
- The Irish are the second worst in the EU at paying their debts, a top business report published on Tuesday said.
- Pulitzer Prize winning author, Irish-American Frank McCourt, is to take up the post of writer-in-residence at the University of Limerick in October.
- Irish firms earned over eight million Irish pounds supplying the international space industry last year.

- Swiss bank Credit Suisse expects European economic and monetary union (EMU) to start on time with at least eight members including Ireland but believes Spain, Portugal and Italy will have to wait for entry in the second round.
